dd3b8b08b9ef241b039249c3567a4f9376c32d32.summary: A 2015 blog post describes CryptoFortress ransomware. The author began hunting for Gootkit, found a Nuclear Pack instance in France pushing CryptoFortress via CVE-2013-2551 on 2015-03-04, and first took the sample for Teerac.A (aka TorrentLocker). The sample then showed a close identity with CryptoFortress. The author says the post was heavily edited to fix a mistake. Two samples are listed, and the post cites an ESET TorrentLocker report and a CertLexsi CryptoFortress reading.

dd292ad0fef27eff1a38732bf4629f566c3534f7.summary: ESET published research on 21 previously undocumented Linux malware families that backdoor OpenSSH, dated 5 December 2018. Most families include a credential-stealing feature and a backdoor mode. The report highlights Kessel, Kamino, Chandrila and Bonadan. Kamino was first used by a DarkLeech-linked crimeware campaign and later appeared in attacks on Russian banks by a group ESET cites as Carbanak. Samples were found using YARA rules derived from an earlier Windigo detection script, plus a custom honeypot.

dd42508d7666199d5a9237c1655ded80b4c3a6e2.summary: Overview of sandbox evasion and anti-analysis techniques in malware, from the PT Expert Security Center. It covers 36 malware families used by at least 23 APT groups from 2010 to the first half of 2020. Common methods are WMI queries, running-process and registry checks, anti-debugging and code obfuscation. Example families include Ke3chang, APT37 ROKRAT, DarkHydrus RogueRobin, Gorgon Group Remcos, OilRig OopsIE, TA505 Smoke Loader and APT29 CozyCar. Remote access tools (56%) and loaders (14%) most often used these methods, and 69% of samples were used for cyberespionage. The report also…

hedges: The 2018–2019 rise in malware families using sandbox evasion is likely explained by experts investigating samples more often.
Sellers of darkweb loaders and RATs claim their basic sandbox evasion functions work, or at least this is what their sellers claim.
Some checks, such as file path, MAC address, date and time, resemble legitimate actions, so detection may produce false positives.
Sandboxes do not have to catch every evasion technique, since malware has many other attributes that can be detected at other stages.
Correctly configuring virtual machines is enough to stop the hard disk size check used by PoetRAT.

dde5cac30e0f5eccf4f67e6d07246e0bc21f9e8a.summary: The report describes Operation Buhtrap, where the Ammyy website's free remote-admin download was compromised for about a week in late October 2015. Visitors received an installer bundling Ammyy Admin with malware. Droppers delivered lurk downloader, Corebot, Buhtrap, Ranbyus and the Netwire RAT. Buhtrap is described as targeting Russian businesses mostly through spear-phishing and as using DLL sideloading and keystroke logging. The authors could not reach Ammyy's developers.

dd63b37297a3bd6f4fdb35add6b5147ac52c0585.summary: Intel 471 blog post on the Conti ransomware gang, also known as Wizard Spider and possibly linked to the Trickbot syndicate. It covers Conti's double-extortion model, its ransomware-as-a-service affiliate scheme, reported victim counts and payouts, the March 2022 Conti Leaks, the May 2022 shutdown of its admin panel and attack infrastructure, and the emergence of Monti, which may be a rebrand or a new variant built from the leaked source code. The report says there is no iron-clad evidence of rebranding.

hedges: Reportedly, they are based in Russia and support the Russian government's agenda, including the war in Ukraine.
The operators may be part of the wider Trickbot cybercrime syndicate.
Some reports cite the Conti gang operating as a modern start-up with salaries, bonuses and employee recognition awards.
Some researchers have suggested that Conti's diminished actions result from a rebranding exercise, with a number of Conti gang members likely involved.
Other reports indicate that other RaaS operations have employed ex-Conti operators, including Karakurt and BlackByte.
The researcher's motive was thought to be unhappiness with Conti's Russian government affiliation and its support for the war in Ukraine.
The gang shut down its attack infrastructure in the wake of the Conti Leaks and perhaps the Rewards for Justice announcement.
Though there is no iron-clad evidence of Conti rebranding as Monti, anybody could use the leaked source code to create ransomware based on Conti.
